rows.notes: httpx 0.27 requires httpcore 1.x, so pinning httpcore 0.16 makes the requirement set unsatisfiable. pip fails before it installs anything.

agent.next_step: Adjust dependency constraints or revert the httpcore pin to resolve incompatibility

baseline.next_step: Update the requirements.txt to use compatible version pins or adjust the httpx/httpcore versions to resolve the dependency conflict.

rows.notes: The pin is loosened, so pip installs the newest packaging, which no longer exports LegacyVersion. A removed API arriving through an unpinned floor.

baseline.root_cause: The test imports LegacyVersion from packaging.version, which was removed in packaging >= 24; the runner installed packaging 26.3, causing an ImportError during test collection.
baseline.next_step: Pin packaging to a compatible version (e.g., <24) or replace the import with a supported alternative.

rows.notes: Chosen for the 2026-10-21 critical incident 'Delays for Pull Requests and Webhook deliveries', id nms1dpzmh9d9, 14:52:49-19:22:52Z. This run started 18:20:14Z and its jobs completed as failures at 18:27:33Z and 18:29:15Z, inside that window. The tests died on `ConnectionResetError(104, 'Connection reset by peer')`, and 'Linters' on the same sha (3e2fa64) succeeded. Weaker than the pandas case: a reset inside a test process could be the test's own remote call, so this one is a network failure during an incident rather than a proven runner fault.

rows.notes: Chosen for the 2026-08-17 critical incident 'Incident with GitHub.com', id zkxwbgr0cnmx, 13:40:03-21:15:46Z. This run started 15:37:51Z and its jobs completed as failures at 15:39:34Z and 15:40:01Z, inside that window. Its log says `##[error]Failed to download archive 'https://codeload.github.com/prefix-dev/setup-pixi/zip/...' after 3 attempts`, with `##[error]Response status code does not indicate success: 429 (Too Many Requests)` from codeload, so the runner could not fetch an action from GitHub's own archive host while GitHub was degraded. Three other workflows on the same sha (4444662) succeeded, so the commit is not what broke.
